features.title: Adapter selection and resolution
features.summary: Selecting, resolving and validating a Workspace's Adapters: the ordered Adapter list, module resolution, identity and API compatibility, registry collisions, Adapter configuration, invalid-set degradation and repair, and the Workbench Adapter management surface.

rules.statement: The manifest's ordered Adapter list is the only selection of active Adapters; UIUX never enables an Adapter by scanning dependencies or the filesystem.
UIUX loads an Adapter only through its manifest, never by scanning package files, by filename conventions or through side-effect registration.
Project-specific Widgets or Catalog metadata come from separately selected extension Adapters, never from forking or mutating a base Adapter while it runs.
UIUX never installs, upgrades or locks Adapter packages and never edits package.json or lockfiles; it only reads resolved package metadata.
For a missing or incompatible Adapter package, the Workbench gives concrete package-manager repair guidance.
UIUX checks an Adapter's declared API version for compatibility before using any of its plugins, Catalog, renderers, providers, styles or design tokens.
An Adapter is identified by its declared ID, never by its package or display name; its resolved module and package version are provenance only.
Two Adapters claiming the same uniquely owned registry key is a blocking Adapter configuration error.
Adapter order never grants first-wins or last-wins override authority; it only sequences otherwise valid installation of providers, styles and design tokens.
UIUX validates an Adapter entry's configuration against the configuration schema the Adapter declares, while the Adapter owns the schema's meaning.
An Adapter that declares no configuration schema accepts no Adapter-specific configuration.
Design-System-specific configuration lives only in an Adapter entry's configuration, never in fields of the UIUX Workspace schema.
UIUX resolves and validates the whole selected Adapter set, including resolution, API compatibility, configuration and collisions, before constructing a Preview Runtime.
Only a fully valid Adapter set is installed: UIUX never skips a failed Adapter or builds a partial authoritative Runtime.
A failure while constructing the Preview Runtime fails the whole construction and keeps no half-installed Runtime.
An Adapter's renderers, providers, styles and design tokens are installed once, when UIUX constructs the Preview Runtime.
A Workspace whose Adapter set is invalid stays open for inspection and repair, including Review, i18n and Adapter configuration editing.
While the Adapter set is invalid, Preview, render and capture, Catalog-dependent authoring and Adapter-dependent formal Evidence are unavailable.
UIUX never assembles a partial authoritative Catalog from the Adapters that did load, though it may show their safely readable manifest metadata for diagnosis.
A structurally valid manifest is written even when its Adapter set is invalid; Adapter validity becomes Workspace diagnostic state, never a silent rollback.
The Workbench manages Adapter selection, order and configuration and shows each Adapter's resolution, package, identity, API, configuration and collision diagnostics.

features.title: Adapter Catalog and Widget integration
features.summary: The Adapter Catalog's authoring metadata for each Widget type: its boundary with Widget plugin definitions, i18n field mappings and their load-time validation, and asset-capable fields.

rules.statement: UIUX authoring metadata, such as labels, groups, icons, editor controls, i18n mappings and documentation hints, belongs to the Adapter Catalog and is never pushed into Widget Core.
Only Config fields that the Catalog maps for i18n accept a translation binding; an ordinary string field is never translation-enabled implicitly.
Declaring a translatable field needs no UIUX annotation in the plugin's Config schema and changes no raw Config type.
UIUX validates every Catalog i18n mapping when it loads the Adapter, and any mismatch invalidates the Adapter instead of producing a View warning.
An i18n mapping is accepted only when UIUX can passively prove from the plugin's own Config schema that the mapped Config field is string-only; any uncertainty is an Adapter load error.
Mapping validation compares declared Property metadata only and never evaluates a Property to infer its type.
UIUX never executes, normalizes, dereferences, rewrites or duplicates a plugin's Config schema, and never treats Catalog metadata as the authority on Config types.
A Config schema that cannot prove a mapped field string-only stays valid for Widget Core; only the UIUX i18n mapping fails.
The Workbench locates translation-result Properties only through the Catalog mapping, never by Property name or by scanning values shaped like translation results.
An interpolation parameter maps only to a readable Property of the same Widget; expressions and cross-Widget lookups are not part of the mapping.
A translation-result Property declares explicit reactive dependencies on the Properties its mapped parameters name.

features.title: Locale resources
features.summary: Authored Locale resources: Workspace ownership of copy, the global key space, the default Locale and a missing default-Locale file, the Review readiness policy for translation gaps, and empty or whitespace-only translation reminders.

rules.statement: The Workspace's Locale files are the canonical source of authored copy and translations for the design specification.
UIUX works without a product repository or an external translation provider and never synchronizes Locale files with one.
All Locales share one global key space, and any View or Widget may reuse a key.
UIUX never prescribes or validates a key-naming convention, prefix or namespace.
UIUX never infers the default Locale from file order, the current selection or which Locale files exist.
UIUX never creates a missing Locale file on its own.
A default Locale without its Locale file is a persistent Workspace configuration error shown in Checks.
While the default Locale's file is missing, the Workbench offers an explicit action to create it.
While the default Locale's file is missing, translation resolution, Locale-dependent Preview and capture, and formal translation Evidence are unavailable.
While the default Locale's file is missing, Workspace and non-i18n View authoring stay usable.
Missing translations, fallback use, unresolved keys and missing interpolation arguments never by themselves block marking a Review ready, even for a translation Review.
Genuine Runtime failures, invalid Views or Variants, incomplete formal evaluation and blocking Workspace resource errors are never downgraded to translation warnings.
The translation summary flags every Locale value that is exactly empty, and every non-empty value that ECMAScript String.trim() empties, as two separate reminder categories.
Reminders cover every discovered Locale file and key, including keys that no View uses, without evaluating any Widget.
The translation table marks each reminder on its Locale and key cell without changing the authored value or the Preview.
Empty and whitespace-only reminders never enter Review Evidence and never add a readiness gate.
Handoff carries no separate reminder list, count or issue report for empty or whitespace-only values.

features.title: Translation runtime
features.summary: Translating authored copy at run time: `$i18n` bindings and their lowering, the RootShell `t` Method with its fallback, markers, placeholder grammar and warnings, the reactive dependency boundary, and how live and formal evaluation collect translation warnings.

rules.statement: An ordinary string in a View's Config is literal copy, never a translation reference.
Switching the Preview Locale never replaces or erases a View's authored translation binding.
Before Widget Core runs, UIUX lowers each translation binding to its literal key in the Catalog-mapped Config field, never to translated text.
Widget Core and Vue renderers acquire no translation semantics.
A child Widget translates by calling the RootShell `t` Method from its own computed Property.
A Vue renderer never receives `t` and reads localized text only from its Widget's Properties.
A localized Widget exposes a structured translation-result Property that calls `t` once and a plain-text Property that projects its text.
The RootShell `t` Method is read-only and writes no State.
The RootShell `t` Method depends only on the effective Locale, never on the sources of interpolation arguments.
Each child Property declares and tracks the dependencies of its own interpolation arguments.
Changing an interpolation argument recomputes only the affected Properties, without tearing down the Runtime or resetting other Widgets' state.
Mandatory Adapter Runtime conformance tests verify the dependency boundary between `t`, translation-result Properties and their parameter Properties.
The `t` Method always returns renderable text with its warnings as a successful result; a recoverable translation problem never fails the Method.
When the requested Locale lacks a key, `t` uses the default Locale's text and warns that it fell back.
When neither the requested nor the default Locale has the key, `t` returns the unresolved-key marker with a warning, never an empty string or the raw key.
A present Locale value that is empty or only whitespace is available copy: `t` returns it unchanged, without fallback, marker or warning.
A placeholder whose argument is absent renders the missing-parameter marker in its place and adds a warning.
An argument supplied as an empty string is present, so it is substituted and never treated as missing.
The `t` Method parses a message once, left to right, and never re-parses escaped text or interpolated values.
A malformed placeholder fragment renders literally, without argument lookup, warning or Method failure, and leaves valid placeholders elsewhere in the message intact.
The unresolved-key and missing-parameter markers are design-time diagnostics and never count as valid production copy.
Preview and the Workbench render `t` text, markers included, verbatim and derive diagnostics only from the structured warnings, keeping no second placeholder state.
Warnings from `t` describe only the translation problem; `t` never receives or reports the View, Variant, Widget or Property.
The Workbench attributes each warning to its View, Variant, Widget, result Property and Catalog field through the Catalog mapping and read-only Widget inspection.
Ordinary Preview reports warnings only for translation Properties the Runtime actually evaluated and never forces hidden or offscreen Widgets to evaluate.
A translation Property that was never evaluated is unverified, and one whose evaluation failed or is missing is incomplete.
A translation Property's live warnings are those of its latest completed result, so each recomputation replaces them.
Changing the Locale, Variant or Runtime clears the live warnings of the previous context.
Within one evaluation context a warning is identified by its Widget, result Property, key, warning code and missing parameter, so the same problem in different Widgets or Properties stays separate.
Formal Review validation and capture evaluate every Catalog-declared translation-result Property of the target View and Variant, including hidden or not-yet-rendered Widgets.
A formal evaluation that cannot evaluate a declared Property records incomplete coverage with the missing occurrences and never claims a complete pass.
Formal translation Evidence never parses, duplicates or normalizes markers into a separate record.

features.title: Checks
features.summary: The Workspace Checks surface: which findings it gathers, how it reports their origin and check state, how it groups, orders and navigates them, and what it leaves out.

rules.statement: Checks lists diagnostic findings only, never Review status, approval queues or tasks.
Checks gathers translation reminders, current Preview translation warnings, structural and schema validation findings, current Runtime errors and Catalog problems of used entries.
Each finding keeps its origin, scope, check state and original severity or blocking meaning; Checks never merges sources into one warning type.
Checks tells apart not yet checked, checking, completed with or without findings, and failed or incomplete, and never shows an unrun check as zero findings.
Opening Checks never runs validation, forces hidden Properties to evaluate or invokes `t`.
Run Checks explicitly produces or refreshes a complete check result, and live background warnings are never presented as a complete run.
Each Run Checks produces a new immutable Evidence record of its result instead of overwriting an earlier one.
Checks never shows a Runtime error from an earlier Preview, Variant or Locale as a current finding.
Listing a blocking structural or executable problem in Checks never weakens its Preview, capture or Review gating.
Historical Review and capture Evidence never merges into the live Checks list.
Checks groups and filters findings by source, category, severity, View and Variant.
By default Checks orders findings by severity, then code or category, then stable View and Widget location.
Selecting a finding opens its exact authoring context: the View, Variant, Widget, file or editor it concerns.
Translation reminders appear in Checks by Locale, key and reminder type and open the matching translation-table cell.
Checks groups translation warnings primarily by warning code, then by key and missing parameter, each group counting and listing its affected Widget and Property occurrences.
Within a translation-warning group, occurrences are ordered by View, Variant, Widget, and Property or Catalog field.
Checks reports Catalog problems only for entries that at least one View uses; problems of unused entries appear only in Catalog management.
One Catalog problem shows once, expanding to each distinct affected View and then each distinct affected Widget, with separate counts at each level.
The affected Views and Widgets of a Catalog problem follow current Workspace usage without revalidating the Catalog.

features.title: Authored Assets
features.summary: Authored Assets: binding them from Views, resolving them for execution, replacing their content, validating their media types, and handling invalid or unused Assets.

rules.statement: UIUX never treats an arbitrary string or Config value as an Asset reference.
For execution UIUX resolves each Asset binding to the value the Adapter's renderer consumes at run time, without changing the authored binding or Widget Core semantics.
Preview receives only an Asset's resolved run-time value and validated media metadata, never a filesystem path.
Replacing an Asset's content keeps its identity, so existing bindings stay valid.
A replacement updates the Asset's source content and its metadata together in one mutation.
A distinct, independently referenced Asset is created with a new identity, never by replacing an existing Asset.
Where determinable, UIUX checks an Asset's declared media type against its content signature and filename extension, and a mismatch is an Asset validation error.
Binding an Asset whose media type or category the Catalog field does not accept is a View validation error.
Missing or corrupt Assets, metadata and content mismatches, missing binding targets and incompatible bindings are diagnosed without rewriting authored data.
A View that binds a missing or invalid Asset cannot render, be captured or produce formal Evidence until it is repaired.
UIUX never substitutes a placeholder or retargets another Asset or path for an invalid binding.
An Asset that no View references stays a valid resource and may be marked unused, but is never removed automatically.

features.title: Content-addressed artifact store
features.summary: The content-addressed store of UIUX-derived artifacts: who produces and reads artifacts, and when they may be removed.

rules.statement: Derived artifacts are created only by producer actions such as capture, checks, Evidence and Handoff export; no Tool or route offers a generic artifact write or overwrite.
Artifacts are read by their content identity, never through a path or a mutable latest name.
Normal capture, check and mutation actions never delete artifacts.
Artifact cleanup is an explicit mark-and-sweep maintenance action that removes only blobs unreachable from surviving Evidence, Review and still-relevant Handoff references.
Artifact cleanup never rewrites a canonical record.

features.title: Render context
features.summary: Render contexts: Workspace-owned viewport and theme registries, Adapter theme validation, and live context switching in Preview.

rules.statement: A theme that the active Adapters do not support is reported as a render-context diagnostic and never replaced by another theme.
Execution uses only theme and viewport IDs that exist in the Workspace registries.
The Workbench may offer convenience viewport presets when one is created, but only presets saved in the Workspace are canonical.
In live Preview, changing the Locale, viewport or theme keeps unrelated interaction state, such as entered values or expanded controls, while the Runtime stays valid.

features.title: Formal Evidence capture
features.summary: Formal Evidence capture: its engine and shared service, the explicit render contexts it runs, Runtime isolation per context, what a capture records, interaction-replay records, and how an Evidence error differs from findings inside Evidence.

rules.statement: Formal capture runs Playwright with Chromium on the server.
HTTP, MCP, the CLI and the Workbench capture through one shared server capture service, and the Workbench never rasterizes the DOM itself.
Formal capture runs an explicit list of resolved render contexts and never expands Variants, Locales, viewports or themes into an implicit Cartesian product.
Convenience selections, such as all current Variants or Locales, resolve into the explicit context list before capture runs.
A capture context without a Variant starts from a fresh deterministic Runtime and never inherits state from an earlier capture context.
Formal capture renders the clean Preview Host, never Workbench Review chrome such as pins, highlights or overlays.
Each capture records the resolved context it actually executed, so a later registry change never alters what existing Evidence says it captured.
Only a corrupt, schema-invalid or unverifiable Evidence record is an Evidence error; warnings inside a valid record are data.
Replaying interaction Evidence records pass or fail for each assertion together with the captures it requires.

features.title: Evidence freshness
features.summary: Whether existing formal Evidence still holds for the current Workspace: the staleness conditions, and which Evidence a change requires regenerating.

rules.statement: A formal capture that names no View, or whose provenance records no View revision, is stale.
A formal capture whose View no longer exists is stale.
A formal capture is stale once its View's current revision differs from the revision it recorded.
A formal capture is stale once its Locale no longer exists in the Workspace.
A formal capture is stale once its Locale's revision differs from the revision it recorded.
A formal capture is stale once its viewport preset is removed.
A formal capture is stale once its viewport preset's width or height differs from the size it captured.
A formal capture is stale once its theme is removed from the Workspace.

A formal capture is stale, with the reason that its Adapter changed since capture, once its recorded Adapter provenance no longer matches the current active Adapter set in selection, order or content.
A formal capture that records no Adapter provenance has unknown freshness, which counts as not fresh.
Which existing Evidence a change requires regenerating is decided from the change's structured change domains, never inferred from prose.
Evidence that a change's domains leave demonstrably unaffected stays valid and need not be rerun.

features.title: Handoff export
features.summary: Handoff export: roots and their dependency closure, bundle immutability, implementation-source references, Adapter and Locale content, and closure-scoped readiness including Review coverage.

rules.statement: Handoff generates no production code.
Canonical resources enter a bundle verbatim in their own source formats, never converted into a second equivalent schema.
An export starts from explicit typed roots, and a View's feature tag is never a root or an export boundary.

A bundle holds the deterministic transitive closure of its roots, including Flow target Views and Variants, bound Assets, applicable Locale files, Adapter and source provenance, and selected formal Evidence.
Whole-Workspace export is a convenience preset that roots every resource of the Workspace.
An Asset or derived artifact that the closure does not reach never enters a bundle.
An exported bundle is immutable, and exporting again creates a new bundle instead of changing an earlier one.
Downstream implementers, human or Agent, consume a bundle read-only, starting from its root manifest and following its references.
A coherent bundle may be exported for a scope that is incomplete, invalid, under-evidenced or not fully reviewed.
Only a bundle whose closure passes the formal readiness gate claims implementation-ready; any other bundle is a diagnostic snapshot that implies no readiness.
Problems outside a bundle's roots and their closure never affect its readiness.
Any blocking problem or missing required Evidence inside the closure prevents the readiness claim.
Each View in the closure needs at least one fresh formal capture with complete coverage before the bundle can claim readiness.
Only fresh formal captures of closure Views enter a bundle as Evidence; stale captures are left out.
Every Review thread anchored to a View in the closure is in the closure.
Every Workspace thread is in the closure of every export, so an unresolved one blocks readiness for every root.
A closure thread blocks the readiness claim only while it is open or ready for review; every resolution counts as closed.
Only a verified resolution counts as an Evidence-checked change; every other resolution counts as closed without one.
Each won't-fix thread in the closure adds a non-blocking advisory diagnostic naming the thread, which never changes readiness.
For every Widget type the closure uses, a bundle makes the Widget plugin's semantic source and its renderer integration traceable, with the referenced Design System source where relevant.
Adapter-provided mappings select the curated sources, and each materializable file is snapshotted by content identity with its original package or repository, revision and path.
A source that cannot or must not be embedded is marked provenance-only or unavailable, never silently dropped.
A bundle records every active Adapter, in Adapter-list order, with its authored selection and resolved provenance.
A local Adapter without a reliable package version is identified by a stable digest over all the Adapter content that took part in resolution and loading.
Adapter provenance is an export-time snapshot and never rewrites the Workspace's Adapter configuration.
A bundle keeps each View's authored translation bindings together with the parameter-name bindings, or their provenance, needed to understand them.
UIUX plumbing for Adapters and translation, such as mapped Property names, translation results and live warnings, is never a production-data contract of a bundle.
Handoff provenance never enters the canonical schemas of the resources it describes.

features.title: Review lifecycle and resolution
features.summary: The lifecycle of a Review thread: ready-for-review submissions and their Evidence gate, resolution and its kinds, reopening, and how the Workbench offers resolution.

rules.statement: Every lifecycle transition appends an immutable event to the thread's history, and the thread's current status always matches the latest one.
Marking a thread ready for review records a new immutable submission; it means work was submitted, not that it was accepted.
Every entry into ready for review, including one after a reopen, appends a new submission and never replaces an earlier one.
Once a submission exists, its change domains, resources and Evidence references never change.
A Widget thread can enter ready for review only while its anchored View is valid as a whole and every named Variant is executable.
A Widget thread's submission names its anchored View at that View's current revision.
A Workspace thread's submission names the current Workspace manifest revision as its subject.
Every View a Workspace thread's submission names must exist, be valid and be named at its current revision.
Every Evidence reference of a submission must name an Evidence record that exists in the Workspace.
Formal-capture Evidence cited by a submission must be complete for the current revision of the View it captured, and that View must belong to the submission's target set.
An Evidence reference whose declared kind differs from the referenced record's kind is invalid and diagnosed, never coerced or rewritten.
A visual or interaction change cites Playwright captures of the clean Preview Host in the affected render and Variant contexts.
A purely textual Spec change needs no capture but still needs passing validation.
An interaction change cites replayable interaction Evidence of structured steps, targets and assertions replayed with Playwright; screenshots alone never verify interaction.
Resolving a ready-for-review thread without naming a resolution resolves it as verified, accepting its latest submission.
Resolving an open thread requires an explicit resolution; the API never chooses one for the caller.
Closing a ready-for-review thread with any resolution other than verified leaves its pending submission in the thread, not accepted.
UIUX never checks a resolution against other resources: whether a thread is obsolete or a duplicate is the resolving human's judgment.
Reopening a thread, whatever its resolution, keeps its earlier lifecycle events and submissions unchanged in its history.
After a reopen, a verified resolution needs a new submission: an earlier verified resolution is never carried forward.
In the Workbench, the one-click Resolve resolves an open thread as answered and accepts a ready-for-review thread's submission as verified, naming that submission.
The Workbench's Resolve menu groups answered and verified under Resolve, and obsolete, duplicate and won't-fix under Dismiss; the grouping is presentation only.
For a thread whose anchor is invalid, the Workbench offers resolving it as obsolete but never chooses that resolution without the user.
The timeline shows each resolution with its kind, and marks a submission declined by a non-verified close as not accepted.

features.title: View Spec Decisions
features.summary: Decisions recorded in a View's Spec: their identity, lifecycle and history, the derived lists of pending Decisions, and explicit promotion of a Review thread into a Decision.

rules.statement: A View's Decisions all live in one list in that View's Spec, whatever their status.
Pending, deferred and decided Decision lists are derived from that one list and never stored separately.
A Decision keeps its identity through every status change; deferring, deciding or reopening never moves or re-creates it.
A Decision's status changes only through explicit lifecycle actions, never implicitly.
Reopening a decided Decision clears its current outcome, and the earlier outcome survives only in its history.
Every status or outcome change appends a history entry recording its time, its actor or source and the state before and after, so a Decision's lifecycle never depends on Git.
The Workbench derives a cross-View list of pending Decisions from the View files and navigates from each item to its View, and to its Variant or Widget when known.
No reply, resolution or reopen of a Review thread changes or settles a Decision.
A Review thread becomes a Decision only through an explicit promotion by a human or Agent; comments are never turned into Decisions automatically.
A thread is promoted only into the View it is anchored to.
A Workspace thread cannot be promoted; it must first be re-anchored to a View's RootShell.
A promoted Decision starts pending unless the promotion records an outcome, which makes it decided.
A promoted Decision records its source thread's identity, and the Workbench navigates from the Decision back to that thread.
Promoting a thread that already has a Decision in its View returns that Decision instead of creating a duplicate.
That idempotent return comes before revision checks, so retrying a committed promotion with its original expected revisions succeeds.
Creating another, independent Decision from the same thread requires a distinct explicit action.
Promotion checks the thread's and the View's revisions and adds the Decision to the View in one atomic commit, leaving the thread unchanged.
Promote and resolve stay two actions with their own revision checks: there is no compound promote-and-resolve action and no promoted resolution kind.
When a promotion conflicts, the Workbench names which resource moved, the thread or the View, re-reads and asks the user to confirm again.

contracts.title: Workspace persisted format
contracts.summary: The persisted format of a UIUX Workspace, versioned as a whole by the manifest `schemaVersion`: the manifest, the path, file unit and identity of every canonical resource kind and of the content-addressed derived-artifact store, the canonical JSON shapes of those resources, and the diagnostics of a Workspace whose schema is older or unsupported.

clauses.statement: The Workspace manifest is `.uiux/workspace.json` under the Workspace root. The `.uiux/` directory is reserved for UIUX system metadata, such as the manifest and the derived-artifact store.

The manifest is a JSON object holding the Workspace-level settings: `schemaVersion`, `i18n`, the ordered `adapters` list and the `viewports` and `themes` registries. All five are required; an empty `adapters` list or registry is valid.

`schemaVersion` is a positive integer and the only schema version in a Workspace: resource files carry none and are all decoded under it. The current version is 3; versions 1 and 2 are recognized older versions.
The migration steps are `uiux.v1-to-v2`, from `schemaVersion` 1 to 2, and `uiux.v2-to-v3`, from 2 to 3.
A field introduced by a later schema version is invalid (`schema.unknown_field`) in a Workspace at an earlier version; no version treats a later version's field as an optional addition.

A Workspace whose schema is `unsupported` is reported with the diagnostic `workspace.schema_unsupported`, which is also the code of every operation refused because of it; an operation refused because the Workspace needs migration reports `workspace.migration_required`. Over HTTP, formal capture, Handoff readiness assessment and Handoff export refused with `workspace.migration_required` answer 422.

`i18n` is an object whose required `defaultLocale` is a canonical BCP 47 tag. Supported Locales are discovered from Locale files and not listed in the manifest, and `i18n` gains further settings only additively, through schema evolution.
View data binds a translation as `{ "$i18n": "<key>" }`, an object whose only member `$i18n` is a non-empty literal key.

`adapters` is an ordered array whose order is the canonical installation order. Each entry holds a portable module reference (a bare package or module specifier, or a `./` specifier relative to the Workspace root; never an absolute or resolved path) and an optional JSON-compatible Adapter `config`.

`viewports` maps viewport IDs to presets. A viewport ID is a non-empty, case-sensitive, opaque Workspace-local string, and each preset records the exact CSS viewport width and height; labels and other metadata are separate from identity.
`themes` maps theme IDs, which are non-empty, case-sensitive, opaque Workspace-local strings, to theme entries; Adapters validate or map those IDs but do not own them.
Each View is one file `views/<uuid>.view.json`, where `<uuid>` is the View's full UUID and equals its `id`.

A View's top level has exactly `id` (its full UUID), `name` (its required display name), an optional single-valued `feature` tag, `ir`, `variants` and `spec`; derived timestamps, file paths or filenames and a generic `metadata` object are not canonical fields.

`ir` is the RootShell Widget, with type `RootShell`, ID `root` and one Slot, `content`: an ordered array of child Widget sources whose own shape the Adapters' Widget plugins define, and which is empty for an empty View.

`variants` is an object keyed by Variant name, a non-empty string. Each entry is `{ state }`, where `state` maps Widget IDs to sparse maps of State member overrides (`variants.<name>.state.<widgetId>.<member>`); entries carry no UUID and do not repeat the name, and the entry object stays open to additive metadata.

`spec` always contains `intent` (a string), `entryConditions`, `interactionRules`, `constraints` and `accessibility` (string lists whose items carry no IDs), `references` (typed references) and `decisions` (Decisions).
Each `references` entry is a typed reference discriminated by `type`, `view` or `external`, with an optional non-empty string `relation`; any other `type` is invalid until a schema version adds it.
A View reference is `{ type: "view", viewId, variantName?, relation? }` with a full View UUID as `viewId`.
An external reference is `{ type: "external", uri, label?, relation? }` with a non-empty absolute URI of any scheme as `uri`.

A Decision is `{ id, question, status, outcome?, history, provenance? }`: `id` is a full UUID, `question` a string and `status` `pending`, `deferred` or `decided`; `outcome` `{ summary, rationale }`, with a non-empty `summary` and a string `rationale`, is present exactly when `status` is `decided`.
A Decision `history` entry is `{ at, actor?, source?, before, after }` with an `actor` or a `source`, where `before` and `after` are `{ status, outcome? }` snapshots.

Each history entry's `before` equals the previous entry's `after` (`decision.discontinuous_history`), and the last entry's `after` equals the Decision's current status and outcome (`decision.history_state_mismatch`).
Decision transitions are `pending` ↔ `deferred`, `pending` → `decided`, `deferred` → `decided` and `decided` → `pending`; a reopen's `before` keeps the prior outcome and its `after` has none.
`provenance`, when present, is a JSON object; a Decision promoted from a Review thread records that thread's ID in it as both `reviewId` and `sourceReviewThreadId`.
Each UX Flow is one file `flows/<uuid>.flow.json`, where `<uuid>` equals the Flow's `id`.

A UX Flow is `{ id, name, scenarioRef?, entryStepId, steps }`: `id` is its full UUID, `name` a required non-empty display name, `entryStepId` the full UUID of one of its steps and `steps` an object keyed by full step UUIDs; there is no top-level `transitions` array.

A step entry is `{ target: { viewId, variantName? }, transitions }` and does not repeat its key as `id`; each transition is exactly `{ trigger: { widgetId, event }, targetStepId }`, with no ID or `sourceStepId`, and transition order carries no meaning.

`scenarioRef`, when present, is a JSON object naming an external system or source and an opaque external ID or URI, optionally with a non-authoritative display label; UIUX does not validate its members.
Each Review thread is one file `reviews/<uuid>.review.json`, where `<uuid>` equals the thread's `id`.

A Review thread is a JSON object with exactly `id` (its full UUID), `anchor`, `variantNames` (an array of unique non-empty Variant names), an optional `displayHint`, `status` and the ordered arrays `messages`, `history` and `submissions`.

`anchor` is either the Widget anchor `{ viewId, widgetId }`, with a full View UUID and a non-empty Widget ID, or the Workspace anchor `{ scope: "workspace" }`. Both arms are closed; an object with `scope` is the Workspace arm, and any other `scope` value is `review.invalid_anchor_scope`.

A Workspace-anchored thread has `variantNames: []` (`review.workspace_anchor_variants`) and no `displayHint` (`review.display_hint_without_widget`); the same holds for the Workspace arm inside re-anchor events.
`status` is `open`, `ready-for-review` or `resolved`.
Every message, message edit, submission and history event records an `actor` `{ type, id?, displayName? }` and an authored time `at`, an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.

A message is `{ id, actor, at, body, edits? }`: `id` is a full UUID and `body` the current text; `edits`, when present, is a non-empty array (`review.message_edits_empty`) of closed `{ id, actor, at, previousBody }` entries, each with a full UUID `id`.

An edited message has an `actor.id`, every edit's `actor` has the message's `actor.id` and `actor.type` (`review.message_edit_not_author`), and edit times strictly follow the message's `at` and never decrease (`review.message_edit_out_of_order`).
No submission and no event entering `resolved` has an `at` between a message's `at` and an edit's `at`, inclusive (`review.message_edit_after_formal_act`).
An edited message's `body` is non-empty after trimming (`review.message_body_empty`).
Each edit's `previousBody` differs from the text that replaced it (`review.message_edit_noop`).

A submission is `{ id, actor, at, changeDomains, resources, scope, evidenceRefs }`: a full UUID `id`, at least one change domain, at least one resource `{ identity, revision }`, a `scope` object and at least one Evidence reference.
A submission's `at` equals the `at` of the lifecycle event entering `ready-for-review` that names it (`review.submission_time_mismatch`).

Each `evidenceRefs` entry is exactly `{ kind, evidence }`: `kind` is the Evidence taxonomy discriminator and `evidence` the referenced immutable Evidence record's `sha256:<hex>` identity; an entry has no ID, label or other metadata.

A history event has a full UUID `id`, `kind` `lifecycle` or `reanchor`, `actor`, `at` and an optional `reason`. A lifecycle event adds `from`, `to`, an optional `submissionId` and an optional `resolution`; a re-anchor event adds `before` and `after`, each `{ anchor, variantNames }`.

Lifecycle transitions are `open` → `ready-for-review`, `ready-for-review` → `open`, `resolved` → `open`, `ready-for-review` → `resolved` with any resolution and `open` → `resolved` with any resolution but `verified`; any other is `review.invalid_transition`, and the first lifecycle event starts from `open` (`review.invalid_initial_status`).

`resolution` is `verified`, `answered`, `wont-fix`, `duplicate` or `obsolete` (`review.invalid_resolution`), present exactly on lifecycle events entering `resolved` (`review.resolution_required`, `review.resolution_unexpected`); a thread's current resolution is that of its final lifecycle event while it is resolved, never stored separately.
An event entering `resolved` with `verified` carries the active submission's `submissionId` (`review.resolve_missing_submission`, `review.resolve_stale_submission`).
An event entering `resolved` with any resolution other than `verified` carries no `submissionId` (`review.direct_resolve_submission_forbidden`).
An event entering `resolved` with `duplicate` has a non-empty `reason` (`review.resolution_reason_required`).
The `actor` of an event entering `resolved` has `type` `human` (`review.resolve_requires_human`).

`displayHint` is a closed object with at least one member (`review.display_hint_empty`); its only member, `pin`, is a closed `{ x, y }` of finite numbers from 0 to 1 inclusive (`review.display_hint_out_of_range`), normalized against the anchored Widget's full rendered rectangle with the origin at its top-left, x rightward and y downward.
Writers clamp pin coordinates to [0, 1] and quantize them to 4 fractional digits; validators check only the range and never repair a value.

Each Locale is one file `i18n/<locale>.json`, named by its canonical BCP 47 tag, holding one flat JSON object that maps literal message keys to string values: `.` in a key has no nesting or namespace meaning, and there are no per-View, split or merged Locale files.
Locale files are discovered from `i18n/*.json`; a file whose name is not a canonical BCP 47 tag is diagnosed and excluded from the discovered Locales, never aliased to or merged with another file.
Each authored Asset is one directory `assets/<uuid>/` containing `asset.json` and exactly one source-content file; the directory UUID equals the `id` in `asset.json`.
`asset.json` records at least the Asset `id`, a required display `name`, the source-content filename and the declared `mediaType`; references never depend on display, original or content filenames.
View data binds an Asset only as `{ "$asset": "<assetId>" }`, and only in Adapter Catalog fields declared asset-capable.
Authored Assets under `assets/` are source data; UIUX-generated derived artifacts live separately under `.uiux/artifacts/`.
A derived artifact is identified by `sha256:<hex>` over its bytes and stored immutably under `.uiux/artifacts/sha256/`: identical bytes deduplicate, and an existing blob is never overwritten.

Formal Evidence records are themselves immutable artifacts in that store; there is no mutable `evidence/` resource namespace, and rerunning Evidence creates a new artifact rather than overwriting one.

A formal Evidence record is canonical JSON `{ schemaVersion, kind, executionContext, coverage, provenance, artifactRefs, evidenceRefs?, data? }` with no `id`: `kind` is its Evidence kind, `coverage.complete` a boolean and `artifactRefs` the `sha256:` identities of artifacts it references.

An Evidence record's `provenance` is `{ workspaceSchemaVersion, resources, versions, gitCommit? }`, where `resources` lists the `{ identity, revision }` of each resource it used and `versions` includes `uiux`.

A formal capture record has `kind` `formal_capture` and schema version 1, its resolved render context as `executionContext`, the View, Workspace manifest and Locale revisions in its provenance, and its PNG screenshot in `artifactRefs`.

A formal capture record's provenance lists every Adapter of the active set in Adapter-list order, each with its authored module specifier, resolved Adapter ID, API version, package version when available, and the content digest a Handoff bundle records for it, computed over all Adapter content that took part in resolution and loading.

A resolved render context is `{ viewId, variantName?, locale, viewportId, viewport: { width, height }, themeId }`: a View UUID, a Variant name or none for the base state, a canonical BCP 47 Locale, a viewport preset ID with the exact size used, and a theme ID.
A formal translation occurrence is `{ occurrence, evaluatedText, warnings }`: the Workbench occurrence, the evaluated text verbatim with any markers, and the result's original `warnings`.
Formal translation occurrences are ordered by View ID, Variant, stable Widget traversal and mapped result Property, each keeping its result's warnings in their original order.

contracts.title: Mutation and revision semantics
contracts.summary: The semantics every canonical mutation shares on every transport (`/api/*`, `/mcp` and the Workbench): opaque content-derived revisions, the required `expectedRevision`, all-or-nothing conflicts that report the current revision, compact mutation results, the meaning of refusal statuses and the refusal codes of Review actions, how the shared result surfaces over HTTP and MCP, and the change events that commits emit to Workbenches.

clauses.statement: Every mutable canonical resource has an opaque revision derived from its canonical content. Reads and queries return it; it is the same across process restarts and changes whenever that content changes, including through an edit made outside UIUX. Callers must not infer meaning from its representation.
Every mutation of an existing resource carries the `expectedRevision` its caller last read for that resource; a Review action carries its thread's.
A create carries no `expectedRevision`. It names or receives the identity of the new resource, and when a resource with that identity already exists it writes nothing and returns `already_exists`.

When the resource's current revision differs from `expectedRevision`, the whole mutation writes nothing and returns a `conflict` result carrying `currentRevision`; the caller must re-read and decide again.

A successful mutation returns its status, `created`, `updated` or `deleted`, and the affected identity. `created` and `updated` also return the new revision and diagnostics; `deleted`, the result of retracting a Review thread, carries no revision. A result never carries the whole Workspace.
A successful mutation result also carries a summary of what changed.
Competing writes are never merged automatically, by implicit merge, CRDT or OT: the later writer gets a conflict and must re-read, retry or rework explicitly.

Refusals are told apart by status: `conflict` means re-read, `blocked` means a precondition refuses the operation, and `locked` means another member holds an edit lease on the resource, so retry later or ask the holder.
A lease refusal is `{ status: "locked", key, code: "resource.locked", message, lock: { kind, key, holder: { nickname, kind }, expiresAt } }`; it names the holder only by nickname and member kind.
A persistence-busy refusal has the code `persistence.busy`; over HTTP it answers 503 with a `Retry-After` header.
Over HTTP the structured result is the JSON response body; `conflict` and `already_exists` answer 409, and `locked` answers 423.
Over MCP a tool returns the structured result as its structured content (and as JSON text), and any outcome other than success is an error result (`isError`).
HTTP and MCP run an operation through the same application service and return the same result for it; only the transport envelope differs.

The change-event stream is the server-sent events route `GET /api/events`. On connect it sends `hello` with the server instance ID; it sends `resource.changed` (kind, key, revision) or `resource.removed` (kind, key) for a resource, `lock.changed` (kind, key) for a lease and `access.changed` for the roster or the member's role, and a heartbeat comment about every 20 seconds.
Marking a thread ready is refused with `review.target_view_missing` when a target View does not exist.
Marking a Widget thread ready is refused with `review.target_view_revision_missing` when its resources lack its View's current revision.
Marking a Workspace thread ready is refused with `review.target_workspace_revision_missing` when its resources lack the current manifest revision.
Marking a thread ready is refused with `review.resource_revision_not_current` when a View it names is not at its current revision.
Marking a thread ready is refused with `review.formal_evidence_not_current` when cited formal-capture Evidence is not complete for its View's current revision.
On a Workspace thread, setting a pin hint is refused with `review.display_hint_without_widget` and promotion with `review.decision_target_unavailable`.

Editing a message is refused with `review.unknown_message` for a message the thread does not have, `review.message_edit_not_author` when the requester is not its author, `review.message_frozen`, naming the submission or resolution that froze it, for a frozen message, `review.message_body_empty` for empty text and `review.message_edit_noop` for unchanged text.

Retraction is refused with `review.retract_not_author` when the requester is not the author of the thread's message, and with `review.retract_engaged` when the thread is engaged, carrying `reason` `status`, `messages`, `history`, `submissions` or `promoted`.
A promotion conflict lists, in `conflicts`, each resource whose revision moved, `review` or `view`, with its key and its expected and current revision.

contracts.title: MCP interface
contracts.summary: The Model Context Protocol surface that Agents use against one selected Workspace: the `/mcp` endpoint and its bearer authentication, the read-only Resources, the discovery, authoring, Review, Evidence, Handoff and lease Tools, and the per-request instructions.

clauses.statement: MCP is served at `/mcp` on the selected Workspace's `uiux dev` server.
A `/mcp` request reaches a Tool or Resource only with a valid member Token.

On `/mcp`, the message of an authentication failure names the fix: create a Token with `uiux token create` and send it as a bearer Token, or, for a Token of another Workspace's roster, create one for this Workspace or run `uiux access copy`.
UIUX advertises no OAuth metadata: every `/.well-known/*` path answers a JSON 404.
On the LAN listener `/mcp` refuses a Token created without the LAN flag with HTTP 403 `auth.lan_not_allowed`.
The per-request server instructions begin with "Authenticated as <nickname> (<kind>, <role>)." for the authenticated member.

MCP Resources are read-only, and no mutation is exposed as a Resource write: the selected Workspace, each View, UX Flow, Locale, Review thread and authored Asset by its canonical key, and each derived artifact by its `sha256:` digest. Reading one that does not exist is a not-found error.

`list_resources` lists, and `search_resources` searches with a non-empty query, the Views, UX Flows, Locales, Review threads and authored Assets, optionally filtered by kind and, for Review threads, by resolution and anchor scope. Both take a required page `limit` and an opaque `cursor`, and each item carries its kind, key, revision, diagnostic count, a kind-specific summary and its Resource URI.

The Review filters of `list_resources` and `search_resources` are `resolution`, a non-empty list of resolution kinds matching only resolved threads whose current resolution is listed, and `anchorScope`, a non-empty list of `workspace` and `view` (any Widget anchor); either filter excludes other resource kinds, and the search term `workspace` matches Workspace threads.

`create_view` creates a View with the canonical empty RootShell IR, no Variants and no Decisions; `update_view_spec` replaces the descriptive Spec fields, keeping Decisions and every non-Spec field; `update_view_structure` replaces the IR and Variants together, keeping the View's identity, name, `feature` tag and Spec.
`update_workspace_settings` updates the manifest-owned Workspace settings (`i18n.defaultLocale`, `adapters`, `viewports` and `themes`) and keeps `schemaVersion`.
`create_locale` creates a Locale file named by a canonical BCP 47 tag and fails if it exists; `update_locale` updates an existing Locale's messages.
`create_flow` creates a UX Flow (identity, entry step and step transition graph) and fails if it exists; `update_flow` updates one, keeping its identity.
`create_asset` creates an authored Asset from its metadata and source content; `replace_asset` replaces an authored Asset, keeping its identity.

The Review tools are `create_review_thread`, `append_review_message`, `reanchor_review_thread`, `set_review_display_hint`, `submit_ready_for_review`, `reopen_review_thread`, `promote_review_to_decision`, `edit_review_message` and `retract_review_thread`; each atomically changes one Review thread (promotion also writes the target View's Decisions).

`resolve_review_thread` stays registered but always refuses: a human member gets `review.resolve_requires_workbench`, an Agent asking for a resolution other than `verified` gets `review.direct_resolve_requires_workbench`, and any other Agent gets `review.resolve_requires_human`.

`capture_formal_evidence` captures formal Evidence for an explicit list of resolved render contexts; `assess_handoff_readiness` assesses explicit Handoff roots without exporting; `export_handoff` exports an immutable Handoff bundle from explicit roots.

`acquire_lock` takes `{ resources: [{ kind, key }] }` with 1 to 16 entries and is all-or-nothing: it returns `{ status: "acquired", leases: [{ kind, key, expiresAt }] }`, or `locked` naming every conflicting lease. `release_lock` takes optional `resources` (omitted means all of the caller's leases), is idempotent and returns the released list.

contracts.title: Adapter interface
contracts.summary: The interface between UIUX and Design System Adapter packages: the Adapter manifest and its API version, configuration schemas, module resolution and uniquely owned registries, the per-Widget Catalog with i18n and asset-capable field metadata and value contracts, and the RootShell State and `t` Method that Adapter Widgets use, with its result, warnings, markers and placeholder grammar.

clauses.statement: An Adapter package exposes one Adapter manifest with `id`, `apiVersion`, `widgetPlugins`, `catalog`, `renderers`, `providers`, `styles`, `tokens` and an optional `configSchema`.
`id` is a non-empty string, unique within the active Adapter set.
`apiVersion` names the UIUX Adapter API version; the current API is version 1, which accepts `1` and `1.<minor>`.
`configSchema`, when present, is a JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 schema: a boolean schema, or an object whose `$schema` is `https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema`.

A bare specifier resolves through Node module resolution with the Workspace root as its origin, and a `./` specifier relative to the Workspace root; either must yield a file-backed module, and a `./` specifier must stay inside the Workspace root.
Widget types, renderer registrations and Catalog Widget entries are each owned by exactly one Adapter of the active set.
The `RootShell` Widget type and its renderer belong to UIUX; an Adapter that registers either is invalid.
`catalog` holds Widget authoring metadata only under `catalog.widgets.<widgetType>`, keyed by the canonical Widget type; the Catalog root is reserved for future Adapter-level metadata.
`catalog.widgets.<widgetType>.i18n.fields.<authorField>` is `{ configField, resultProperty, textProperty, params? }`, keyed by the canonical translatable authoring field.

`configField` names a top-level raw Config member holding the literal key, `resultProperty` a read-only computed translation-result Property, `textProperty` a read-only computed string Property, and `params` maps parameter names to readable Properties.
Within one Widget's i18n mapping the `configField`, `resultProperty` and `textProperty` names are unique and non-conflicting, and every `params` key matches the placeholder name grammar.

A `resultProperty` declares the value contract `deviltea.uiux/translation-result@1` and a `textProperty` `deviltea.uiux/string@1`, compared by exact string equality; parameter source Properties need no UIUX value contract.
Both value-contract IDs are opaque exact strings; an incompatible change to either value shape gets a new ID, never a reused one.

UIUX accepts a `configField` only when the plugin declares Config with a schema whose direct `properties[configField]` has `type` `"string"` or `["string"]`; boolean, untyped, union, `$ref`, conditional and composed forms fail closed.
`catalog.widgets.<widgetType>.assetFields.<authorField>` is `{ acceptedMediaTypes?, acceptedCategories? }` and declares at least one non-empty list of accepted media types or categories.
RootShell exposes the read-only State members `locale`, `viewport` `{ id, width, height }`, `themeId` and `variantName`, which is `null` for the base state.
RootShell's `t` Method takes a key string and an optional `Record<string, string>` of interpolation arguments; omitting the arguments is identical to passing `{}`.
`t` returns `TranslationResult` `{ text, warnings }`, with `text` a string and `warnings` an array of `TranslationWarning`.

`TranslationWarning` is the closed union `missing-translation` `{ code, key, requestedLocale, fallbackLocale }`, `unresolved-key` `{ code, key, requestedLocale }` and `missing-parameter` `{ code, key, requestedLocale, parameter }`; another code needs a contract extension.
The unresolved-key marker is `⟦missing:<key>⟧` and the missing-parameter marker is `⟦missing-param:<name>⟧`; both are fixed and language-independent.
A placeholder name matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`.
A valid name enclosed by n matching braces renders ⌊n/2⌋ literal brace pairs around the name itself when n is even, or around its argument or missing-parameter marker when n is odd.
A brace run whose opening and closing depths differ, that is incomplete, or that encloses an invalid name is one malformed fragment kept verbatim, and parsing resumes at the next character after it.

`warnings` lists the lookup warning first, then one `missing-parameter` warning per distinct absent name in order of its first interpolating occurrence; an `unresolved-key` result has no `missing-parameter` warnings.
The Workbench wraps each warning as an occurrence `{ warning, viewId, variantName?, widgetId, resultProperty, catalogField }`.

contracts.title: Handoff bundle
contracts.summary: The read-only bundle that downstream implementers consume: the root manifest and its identity, roots, resource snapshots, artifact, Evidence and implementation-source references, provenance including Adapter provenance, and machine-readable readiness, coverage and diagnostics.

clauses.statement: The root manifest is a JSON object `{ schemaVersion, bundleIdentity, exportedAt, roots, resources, artifactRefs, evidenceRefs, implementationReferences, provenance, readiness }`, where `schemaVersion` is the manifest schema version, currently 1, and `exportedAt` an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.
`bundleIdentity` is the `sha256:` identity of the canonical JSON of the manifest without `exportedAt` and `bundleIdentity`, and an export stores the canonical manifest bytes as an artifact.

`roots` is a non-empty list of distinct typed roots, `{ type: "workspace" }`, `{ type: "view", viewId }`, `{ type: "flow", flowId }` or `{ type: "asset", assetId }` with full UUIDs; no other root type exists.

Each `resources` entry is `{ type, identity, revision, snapshot, contentDigest? }`, holding a closure resource's canonical content and export-time revision; an Asset entry's `snapshot` is its `asset.json`, and its `contentDigest` the source content's `sha256:` identity.
Each `artifactRefs` entry is `{ kind, artifact, context? }`, naming a distinct `sha256:` artifact with its kind and the context needed to interpret it.
Each `evidenceRefs` entry is an Evidence reference `{ kind, evidence }` to an Evidence record included in the bundle.
Each `implementationReferences` entry names one used Widget type as `widgetType`, with `semanticSource`, `rendererSource` and optional `designSystemSource` and `supportingSources`.

A source reference is `{ availability, provenance, contentDigest? }` with `availability` `materialized`, `provenance-only` or `unavailable` and a non-empty `provenance`; a materialized source names its package or repository, revision and path and carries its `contentDigest`.

`provenance` is `{ workspaceSchemaVersion, scope, resources, contexts, versions, adapters, gitCommit? }`: `scope` repeats the roots, `resources` lists every resource's identity and revision, `contexts` the resolved render contexts of included Evidence, and `versions` the producing tool versions, including `uiux`.

Each `provenance.adapters` entry is `{ moduleSpecifier, adapterId, apiVersion, moduleIdentity, packageVersion?, contentDigest? }` with a `packageVersion` or a `contentDigest`, and `adapterId`s are unique.

`readiness` is `{ implementationReady, coverage: { validation, evidence, review }, blockingDiagnostics }`, where `implementationReady` is a boolean that is never `true` while any diagnostic has `blocking: true`.
Each `blockingDiagnostics` entry is `{ code, message, blocking, path? }`; advisory entries share the list with `blocking: false`.

`coverage.validation` and `coverage.evidence` are each `{ complete }` with a boolean `complete`: `coverage.validation.complete` states that the closure is valid, and `coverage.evidence.complete` that every closure View has its required Evidence.

`coverage.review` is `{ complete, threads, workspaceThreads, resolved }`: `complete` is false while a closure thread is unresolved, `threads` counts closure threads, `workspaceThreads` the Workspace threads among them, and `resolved` maps each resolution kind to its count.
An unresolved closure thread is the blocking diagnostic `handoff.unresolved_review_thread`, and a `wont-fix` thread the advisory `handoff.review_declined`.
